newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel troops kill Arab in Gaza, unrest in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel troops kill Arab in Gaza, unrest in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops shot dead a Palestinian teenager on Wednesday in clashes over a disputed strip of land near a Jewish settlement bloc in PLO-ruled Gaza, hospital sources said.

In the West Bank town of Hebron, Israeli troops showered with stones and firebombs shot rubber bullets and live ammunition, wounding 37 Arabs as residents observed a general strike called to protest against anti-Moslem posters depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig.
"Maher al-Assar, 16, of Deir el-Balah arrived at Shifa hospital at 1 p.m. (1000 GMT) dead as a result of being shot with live ammunition in the chest," said Dr Moawia Hasanein.
Soldiers shot the boy as Palestinians demonstrated near the Gush Qatif settlement bloc after Jewish settlers began work on a strip of land Arabs said belonged to them, witnesses said.
The Israeli army said the disputed land lay in an area under full Israeli security and civilian control.
"Stones were thrown at an Israeli army force...the army responded with measures to disperse demonstrations," the army said in a statement.
"The situation is very bad and the Israeli army is behaving as if this is an Israeli military base," Khaled Abu Al-Oula, Palestinian military liaison chief in southern Gaza, told Reuters.
He said six other Palestinians were wounded in Gaza.

In Hebron, Israeli snipers deployed across rooftops and alleyways along the dividing line between Israeli-and PLO-controlled sectors of Hebron to confront dozens of youths hurling stones and firebombs.
The youths said they were protesting against the pasting of posters on Palestinian shops on Saturday desecrating Islam's Prophet Mohammad and the holy Koran.
U.S. Consul-General Edward Abington and Palestinian West Bank Preventive Security Chief Jibril Rajoub made their way towards the confrontation line in a bid to calm tensions.
"Concerning the posters, we condemn and deplore anything that ridicules any religion. It was an affront to anyone who respects peoples' religion," Abington said.
Israeli police are holding a 25-year-old Jewish woman suspected of gluing the posters to some 20 Hebron storefronts.
Israeli leaders have repeatedly condemend the posters.
PLO police did not intervene to halt the unrest.
"Security coordination is at a very low level and the outcome of such coordination is bad," Israeli army Hebron commander Colonel Gadi Shamni told reporters.
Palestinian police sources said they feared youths would use policemen as a protective shield, drawing fire in their direction, which could escalate the unrest.
"We are not responsible for protecting (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's policies against our Palestinian people," Rajoub said.
Israeli troops have clashed with Palestinians almost daily since Israel began work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem last March, plunging peacemaking into crisis.
Hebron Mayor Mustafa al-Natshe accused settlers and soldiers of pushing Palestinians towards confrontations.

"The settlers in the city are continuous troublemakers in the city. When the situation becomes quiet, they start acting to provoke the people and unfortunately the Israeli soldiers don't prevent the settlers from harasing people, they encourage them," Natshe said.

In a deserted home behind the confrontation lines in Hebron, dozens of Palestinians running a makeshift assembly line funneled petrol stored in a large bin into empty cola bottles and topped them off with a bit of cloth.
Teenagers lit the homemade molotov cocktails and ferried them to the frontlines to be hurled at Israeli troops.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule in January but troops stayed on to guard 400 Jewish settlers who live in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
